item.title: Algorithmic management and gig workers' workplace wellbeing: the moderating role of psychological resilience
item.description: This study examines how algorithmic management in the gig economy is related to gig workers' workplace wellbeing. Specifically, we explore how algorithmic management corresponds with (positive) challenge appraisal and (negative) threat appraisal. We also examine the moderating role of psychological resilience in these relationships, as well as the implications of appraisal processes for workplace wellbeing. item.description: Artificial intelligence, digital infrastructures, and data-driven systems are reshaping not only strategic capabilities but also the cognitive, motivational, and identity-related conditions that contribute to social cohesion and societal resilience. item.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Cognitive Scaffolding, Substitution, and the Risk of Deskilling
item.description: Abstract The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has raised fundamental questions about its effects on critical thinking and cognitive development. item.description: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence into higher education has outpaced the development of pedagogical frameworks and institutional policies, raising fundamental questions about the purposes of education in an algorithmic age. item.title: AI in education: boosting productivity or challenging cognitive effort?
item.description: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping higher education by changing how students learn and perform academic tasks. Although AI is associated with greater time efficiency and improved academic performance, its broader effects on student productivity and cognitive effort remain insufficiently understood. item.title: Exploring Digital Competence Configurations and Attention Performance Through fsQCA and Machine Learning
item.description: Digital competence among bank employees is an increasingly critical determinant of task efficiency in technology-driven financial service environments. In this study, a hybrid analytical approach is used that combines Fuzzy-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) with ten machine learning (ML) classifiers. item.description: The article examines the shift in the digital cultural ecosystem triggered by the widespread adoption of Generative AI. item.title: Between Human and Machine: University Teachers’ Accounts of Judgment, Metacognitive Defense, and Cognitive Offloading in Generative AI Use
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) allows university teachers to delegate cognitive work while deciding how students should engage with it. Using codebook thematic analysis, we examined multi-source accounts from 25 teachers recruited through an AI-focused learning community and its professional networks in China. item.title: AI as Market Infrastructure: How Misinformation and Automation Inequality Shape Democratic Performance and Economic Wellbeing
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the market-organizing infrastructures that coordinate exchange, reshaping consumer information environments and the allocation of economic value. Drawing on marketing systems theory and consumer emancipation scholarship, we theorize perceived misinformation threat and perceived automation inequality as system-level diagnostics that erode perceived democratic performance and, through it, consumers’ perceived economic wellbeing. item.description: This paper examines knowledge-capital expansion under modern conditions, with particular attention to the transformation of public knowledge into recursively expanding epistemic capacity. item.title: AI-Assisted Translation Pedagogy for Critical Thinking: A Pathway to Sustainable Education
item.description: In the era of artificial intelligence (AI), sustainable education requires not only the integration of advanced technologies but also the cultivation of key competencies such as critical thinking. item.description: ABSTRACT. item.description: Smoking cessation remains a complex self-regulatory challenge, often undermined by cue-triggered cravings arising from habitual, emotional, and social contexts. Existing wearable cessation systems are largely reactive, detecting smoking events only after lapses occur and thus missing the critical window for timely intervention. item.description: This article investigates the current state and foreseeable trajectory of artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on its principal application domains and the governance challenges they raise. item.description: This study examines the relationship between digital distraction and academic self-regulation among distance education students.
